t: #2334 Subarray With Elements Greater Than Varying Threshold — Editorial
o:
We need a contiguous window of size k where EVERY element exceeds threshold/k, i.e., min(window) × k > threshold (integer-exact form of min > threshold/k). Any valid size is acceptable; return -1 if none.

In example 1, [3,4,3] has min 3 and 3×3 = 9 > 6. In example 2, [8] alone works since 8 > 7.

Two classical techniques apply: a monotonic stack that finds, for each element acting as the minimum, the maximal window where it is the minimum; or union-find activating elements from largest to smallest and checking component size × value.
k: Condition ⇔ min(subarray) × k > threshold, so it suffices to consider each element as the minimum of its maximal window.
Monotonic stack: when an element is popped by a smaller/equal value, its window spans between the new stack top and the current index.
Union-Find alternative: activate values in decreasing order; when a component of size s with minimum v satisfies v·s > threshold, s is an answer.

a.i: Keep a stack of indices with strictly increasing values. When nums[i] ≤ nums[top], pop j: j's maximal-minimum window is (stackTop, i) exclusive, of length k = i - stackTop - 1. If nums[j]·k > threshold, return k. Flush the stack at the end with i = n.
s: Iterate i from 0 to n inclusive.
While stack non-empty and (i == n or nums[top] ≥ nums[i]): pop j, compute k = i - prevTop - 1, test nums[j]*k > threshold.
Push i otherwise; return -1 after the flush.
a.t: O(n) — each index is pushed and popped at most once.

a.i: Activate cells from largest value down. Each active cell unions with active neighbors; a component's size tracks the largest window whose minimum is the just-activated value (all members ≥ it). If value × size > threshold, that size is valid.
s: Sort indices by value descending; init DSU with size 0 and active flags.
Activate index i, set size 1, union with active i-1 and i+1.
After unions, if nums[i] × size(find(i)) > threshold return that size; else -1.
a.t: O(n α(n) + n log n) — sorting indices dominates; DSU operations are near-constant.
a.sp: O(n) for parent, size, and order arrays.

w: Use the monotonic stack — it is shorter, O(n), and a template worth memorizing (same family as largest rectangle in histogram). Pitfalls: overflow in nums[j]·k (values up to 1e9 × 1e5 — use 64-bit), and using strict vs. non-strict popping inconsistently (either works since any valid window is acceptable). Follow-up: return the longest such subarray, or count all valid subarrays.
